book.title: Criticulous: The RNG Hellscape
invariants: No convenient amnesia as a continuity device.

render_values.user_prompt:
﻿You are outlining a LitRPG isekai comedy with a fast, forward-motion voice and tight prose. The tone is punchy, absurd, and game-aware, with real stakes hiding inside jokes. The story centers on Arthur “Artie” Penhaligon, an office drone who dies in a vending machine accident and wakes in a System-run character creation void. He accidentally dumps all 100 stat points into Critical Hit Rate (chips grease + UI glitch), locking himself into a “Crit or Quit” build: 1 HP, 100% crits. His snarky System Guide, Fizz, becomes his ally and foil. The world worships RNG and crits; the System is both deity and antagonist. Threads: The 100% Crit Glitch (THREAD_CRIT_EXPLOIT), Vane’s Rivalry (THREAD_VANE_RIVALRY), System Stability (THREAD_SYSTEM_GLITCH), The Ascension / First Glitch Myth (THREAD_THE_ASCENSION). Main cast: Artie, Fizz, Vane (antagonist paladin), Mayor of Oakhaven (NPC power broker), System Administrator (overarching villain).

High-detail story synopsis (chapter by chapter):

Chapter 1 — “Welcome to the RNG-Hellscape” (hook, high intensity):
Artie fights a vending machine for chips, gets electrocuted, and wakes in the Character Creation Void. The System UI mocks him while he allocates stats; grease causes a catastrophic mis-allocation into Crit. The System locks him at 1 HP / 100% Crit and spawns him into the tutorial forest. He immediately faces a hyper-aggressive slime, whiffs repeatedly, then vaporizes it with an absurd crit. The System awards him a cursed “Participation Trophy” item that attracts monsters. He flees, reaches Oakhaven’s gates, and discovers guards betting on crit-rates. Artie is flagged as an anomaly. Inside, he learns crits are social currency. A high-level paladin, Vane, notices the anomaly aura and “mentors” (bullies) him, establishing a rival and power gap. End: Artie barely escapes a forced duel; the world now knows his name.

Chapter 2 — “The Glass Cannon’s Guide to Not Dying” (setup, tactical survival):
Artie tries to sell the cursed trophy but discovers it’s soul-bound. Fizz reveals a loophole in a “Starter Pack” quest; Artie crits a lock, exploding it into gold dust and steals a high-tier evasion cloak (“Cloak of the Cowardly Lion,” +50 Evasion, -100 Dignity). He enters the Low-Level Crypts where enemies move in predictable turn-based rhythms. A skeleton archer triggers a cloak-evasion backflip. Artie discovers his crits overload the system, converting enemies into loot pinatas—he can farm at absurd speed. Vane shows up with a full party, clears rooms effortlessly, and leaves behind a Boss Trigger. Artie decides to summon the Floor Guardian for massive XP, despite his 1 HP fragility.

Chapter 3 — “Math-Boss vs. The Glitch” (pressure, boss fight):
Artie kites the Bone Golem through the crypt, crit-punching armor while stamina drains. Fizz discovers the boss has Crit-Resist, making Artie’s core weapon useless. Artie attempts a physics glitch—critting the floor—collapsing it and trapping the Golem. He charges a heavy attack; the System rolls a “Cosmetic Crit,” turning the Golem into porcelain teacups. The System panics, XP recalculates, and Artie jumps five levels, becoming a Level 10 anomaly. Loot reveals a Ring of the Gambler (double crit damage, every 20th hit self-crits). A mural hints at a “First Glitch.” Artie exits the crypt to find Vane waiting; Vane realizes Artie stole his kill, setting up a chase to the capital.

Chapter 4 — “The Capital of Crits” (investigation, social navigation):
Artie hides in a city that worships RNG—the Temple of the D20, priests praying for high rolls. He seeks a “Stat-Wiper” but learns it’s illegal, punishable by deletion. Fizz leads him to a black-market of “Dev-Haters” selling illegal mods; Artie gets a Lag-Switch potion. He learns Vane is the son of the High Priest of RNG, elevating the rivalry to holy war. A System Sentinel raid forces Artie to use the potion; he escapes but speaks in binary for an hour. The Grand Crit-Off tournament flyer promises a “Shield of Infinite Health.” Artie registers under “Crit-iculous,” accidentally pays all his gold, and must win to survive. Vane sees the roster and smiles. End: tournament confrontation locked.

Chapter 5 — “The Tournament of Tiers” (trial, spotlight):
Artie defeats a tank by critting his belt buckle, disqualifying him. The System introduces wind resistance; Artie must time punches with gusts. He wins by critting the air into a vacuum. In the quarter-finals, he faces a dodge-build rogue; neither can hit for ten minutes. He lures arena-flies using the cursed trophy, lands a crit, and the trophy begins glowing with dark energy (System glitch thread advances). The System warns him for exploitation and applies a random debuff: inverted controls. Artie moonwalks through AOE fireballs, crits a mage’s staff into a rubber chicken, and advances. Vane watches, holding a black-market System Override scroll—final fight is rigged.

Chapter 6 — “The Final Roll” (climax, system-level break):
Vane arrives in reflective legendary armor; Artie’s crits would self-crit. Vane uses the override to disable Artie’s evasion; he becomes a 1 HP target with no dodge. Fizz sacrifices her Guide status to hack arena gravity, giving Artie a 3D movement window. Artie realizes he must crit the Reflect buff itself, not Vane. He lands a meta-crit that causes recursive reflection math. The arena pixelates; the System destabilizes. Vane panics; Artie’s final crit deletes Vane’s character data (not his person). The System Administrator appears to delete Artie. Artie crits the Admin’s Delete button, freezing reality. Fizz rewrites location data; they escape into a Safe Mode world. Aftermath: Artie wakes in a wireframe Null-Zone; his HP reads “NaN,” implying he’s become a virus.

Chapter 7 — “Rebooting for the Sequel” (aftermath, series hook):
Artie adapts to the Null-Zone, eating data packets. Fizz reveals the only fix is reaching the world’s central Server Room. Artie tests NaN HP by cliff-jumping—he clips and respawns. A faction of Beta-Testers finds him and reveals Vane has been upgraded into a Patch-Hunter. Artie receives a legendary quest: “Delete the Admin.” The team heads to the Glitch-Woods. Artie jokes about better drop rates and steps into a portal. End of Book 1, sequel hook locked.

Deliverable: produce a full outline consistent with the above synopsis, preserving the LitRPG/isekai/comedy tone, the crit-glitch power fantasy, and the System-as-antagonist thread. Keep pacing high and transitions causal; ensure each chapter escalates stakes or scope.
